- No functional or documentation changes in this version.

- Improved reply guidelines to require a more authentic, conversational human voice and allow for real emotion and admission of uncertainty.
- Added a prohibition on starting replies with certain formulaic phrases (e.g., "Absolutely", "Certainly").
- Introduced a new human voice reference document and mandated reading it before drafting replies.
- Removed the obsolete skill-card.md file.
- No workflow or feature changes—focus is on higher-quality, more human responses.

Version 1.0.4 of x-reply-unreplied

- No file changes detected in this version.
- No updates to features, workflow, or skip conditions.
- No changes to documentation or user-facing functionality.

- Now requires liking the post before drafting or replying in each candidate thread.
- Updated workflow steps to include the new like action before reply.
- No other workflow or skip/reporting requirements changed.

- Clarified that X (Twitter) must be opened using openclaw managed chrome.
- Added a strict rule: never refresh or reload the notifications page; use only clicks and the back button to navigate.
- Updated the workflow and completion steps for clearer tab management, requiring immediate closure of all x.com tabs after completion.
- Improved wording to emphasize sequential thread processing and stricter navigation discipline.

- Clarified and emphasized that all replies must be 1–2 short sentences; this rule is now marked "CRITICAL NON-NEGOTIABLE."
- Explicitly stated that relaxing the reply length is never allowed unless the user directly requests longer replies.
- Added new "CRITICAL NON-NEGOTIABLE" instructions to process only one thread at a time and to fully finish handling each thread before moving to the next.
- No changes to core workflow or reply criteria.

- Initial release of x-reply-unreplied skill.
- Allows users to efficiently answer X (Twitter) mentions or thread replies that still need a response.
- Handles up to 5 relevant reply opportunities per run by default.
- Replies use a short, first-person, on-topic style (1–2 sentences).
- Includes guidance on when to skip replying (e.g., abuse, spam, or already answered).
- Provides a completion report summarizing actions taken, replies sent, and items skipped.
